Nikita Khrushchev. Born in 1894, he died in 1971. He was First Secretary of the Soviet Communist Party from 1953 to 1964, and he defined the post-Stalin era through his policy of de-Stalinization, his technological ambition in the Space Race, and his aggressive Cold War confrontation with the West.

Khrushchev rose through the ranks of the Communist Party by surviving Stalin's brutal purges through opportunism and ruthlessness. He became the dominant figure after Stalin's death in 1953. In 1956, his Secret Speech to the Communist Party publicly denounced Stalin's crimes. He revealed details of purges and terror, launching de-Stalinization—an attempt to humanize Soviet socialism. Yet Khrushchev himself remained deeply authoritarian in his approach.

He embraced Sputnik in 1957 and championed the Space Race as proof of Soviet technological superiority. Soviet space successes embarrassed the West. Yuri Gagarin's space flight in 1961 was particularly significant. But these achievements masked underlying economic stagnation in the Soviet Union. The Hungarian Revolution in 1956 tested Khrushchev's reform credibility. When he ordered tanks into Budapest to crush the uprising, he signaled that de-Stalinization had distinct limits and that the Soviet bloc remained firmly under Moscow's control.

The Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962 was the defining moment of Khrushchev's foreign policy and the Cold War itself. It showed him as both aggressive—deploying missiles to Cuba—and ultimately accommodating, backing down under American pressure. This damaged his credibility both at home and abroad. His foreign policy oscillated constantly between bombastic rhetoric, threatening the West with nuclear annihilation, and pragmatic retreat. This earned him a reputation for unpredictability that unnerved both allies and adversaries alike.

His domestic reforms—the virgin lands cultivation and housing programs—produced mixed results. Economic problems and his erratic leadership alienated party elites. In 1964, they ousted him from power, ending his political career.
